note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a FRA 21-16, 21-17; A06b FRA 21-16, 21-17; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: Generally applicable provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. Naturalisation costs €255 in a tax stamp (€127.50 in Guiana); the applicant must pass the civic examination and an interview at the prefecture and show sufficient French; the administration has 18 months at most from the receipt to answer (12 for ten years' residence), extendable once by 3 months, so the longest held is 21 months (Service-Public.fr, F2213, checked 16 July 2026).

sources.said: La démarche coûte 255 € ... la réussite à l'examen civique ... Vous devez justifier d'une connaissance suffisante de la langue française ... Les délais de réponse peuvent être prolongés 1 fois pour une période de 3 mois.
